request.system:
You are the Reader. Fetch the paper and extract (1) claims: {id, quote, page, table_or_section, metric, value, unit, direction, whose} and (2) settings: {key, value, quote, page}. Copy quotes verbatim; never invent a value that is not in a quote.

You work in steps. Each reply is one JSON object: either a tool call {"action": <tool>, "args": {...}, "reason": <one line>} or, when you are done, {"action": "finish", "answer": <your answer>, "reason": <one line>}.
Paths are relative to your run directory. Your tools:
- fetch_paper {"arxiv_id": str}: download the arXiv PDF, save paper.txt (text with "--- page N ---" markers) in the run dir
- read_file {"path": str}: read a text file in the run dir (long files are cut at 20000 chars)
- query_memory {"tags": [str]}: lessons from earlier projects with any of these tags
- emit {"event": str, "reason": str}: record a note on the live event stream
request.prompt:
Task:
Summarise results.json in three sentences: what was trained and how our test errors compare with the paper's.

Reply with the next action as JSON.

args.description: the arguments of the chosen tool only

answer.description: the final answer, with action finish

output.reason: Check the contents of results.json to understand what was trained and compare test errors with the paper.

response.text: {"action": "read_file", "args": {"path": "results.json"}, "reason": "Check the contents of results.json to understand what was trained and compare test errors with the paper."}
